prs.title: [compiler] Fix refs false positive for IntersectionObserver callbacks
prs.author: akasakariko
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes #35982

This pull request resolves a false positive ref access error during render when passing callbacks to the global `IntersectionObserver` constructor

Cumulative implementation:
- Both TypeScript and Rust compiler backends model the global `IntersectionObserver` constructor with a deferred frozen callback (`Effect.Freeze`), read-only options (`Effect.Read`), and a mutable non-aliasing return value
- `NewExpression` instructions reuse standard call-effect ref validation rather than branching to a separate path, ensuring unknown constructors receiving refs directly or via callbacks are rejected during render

Review follow-up updates:
- Switched generic return type from `BuiltInObject` shape to `Poly` (`Type::Poly` in Rust and `{kind: 'Poly'}` in TypeScript)
- Updated Rust constructor section heading comment in `compiler/crates/react_compiler_hir/src/globals.rs`
- Simplified positive compiler fixture `allow-ref-access-in-intersection-observer.ts` to two minimal hooks covering construction with and without options
- Retained original `useCallback`, `useMemo`, and options reproduction as an ESLint integration test in `packages/eslint-plugin-react-hooks/__tests__/ReactCompilerRuleTypescript-test.ts`
- Added compiler negative fixture `error.invalid-ref-in-unknown-constructor.js` for passing a direct ref argument to an unknown constructor
- Added compiler negative fixture `error.invalid-mutate-hook-value-in-intersection-observer.js` for mutating a `useMemo`-re

prs.title: Fix overlapping replay slots after a prerender abort
prs.author: gnoff
prs.body:
## Summary

A prerender can abort during a retry after the retried task has spawned a suspended child. Abort cleanup records a replay slot for the whole task, then tries to record a child slot at the same key path. Resuming the parent already renders that child, so the existing assertion turns a resumable abort into a prerender error. This surfaced after the abort unwind change in #37710.

Keep the parent slot and ignore the redundant child slot. The regression test verifies that both children render after resuming.

## How did you test this change?

- `yarn test ReactDOMFizzStaticBrowser --runInBand` (36 passed)
- `yarn test ReactDOMFizzStaticBrowser --prod --runInBand` (36 passed)
- `yarn linc`
- `node scripts/prettier/index.js check-changed`

prs.title: Revert sync abort replay restoration pending a complete fix
prs.author: gnoff
prs.body:
Revert #37710 and #37850 while we revisit how synchronous prerender aborts preserve replay state.

Restoring the aborted task root as a replay point can overlap postpones from child tasks. #37850 suppresses one form of the overlap, but an indexed parent slot can still coexist with a descendant replay node and fail during resumption. This removes the incomplete change so we can address the replay invariants together.

This deliberately restores the behavior reported in #37709: if a prerender abort interrupts a task after it has rendered part of its shell, the later resume can omit that markup. That regression needs a follow-up fix.

This supersedes #37851.

Tests: `yarn test ReactDOMFizzStaticBrowser --runInBand` and `yarn test ReactDOMFizzStaticBrowser --prod --runInBand` (34 passed in each mode).

prs.title: [release] Await gh availability check before verifying artifacts
prs.author: irontaek
prs.body:
## Summary

`executableIsAvailable` in `scripts/release/shared-commands/download-build-artifacts.js` is `async`, but `processArtifact` calls it without `await`:

```js
if (executableIsAvailable('gh')) {
  await exec(`gh attestation verify artifacts_combined.zip --repo=${REPO}`, ...);
}
```

The condition is a `Promise`, so it is always truthy. On a machine without the `gh` CLI the script still runs `gh attestation verify` and fails, instead of skipping verification as the check intends. This adds the missing `await`.

## How did you test this change?

The helper is not exported, so I reproduced it standalone with the same implementation and a command that isn't installed:

```console
$ node repro.js
without await: branch taken
with await:    skipped
```

The diff is the single `await`; `processArtifact` is already `async`.
